K1.name: Law scales
K1.caption: Picture weighing every use of personal data against the law.

K2.name: The organisation rulebook
K2.caption: Open the rulebook before handling organisational data.

K3.name: The lifecycle wheel
K3.caption: Follow the wheel from planning through preparation and analysis to communication, then refine.

K4.name: Four data drawers
K4.caption: Recognise open, public, administrative and research data; these types can overlap, and sensitivity is a separate question.
K4.svg: <rect x="10" y="11" width="20" height="19" rx="3"/><rect x="34" y="11" width="20" height="19" rx="3"/><rect x="10" y="34" width="20" height="19" rx="3"/><rect x="34" y="34" width="20" height="19" rx="3"/><path d="M17 20h6m18 0h6M17 43h6m18 0h6"/>

K5.name: Grid and loose threads
K5.caption: Compare an ordered table with free-form content before choosing how to analyse it.

K6.name: The database blueprint
K6.caption: Design the tables, keys and relationships behind the stored data.

K7.name: A user-centred compass
K7.caption: Let the user and their domain guide what useful and accessible analysis looks like.

K8.name: Warning in the table
K8.caption: Scan the table for quality risks before trusting the result.

K9.name: The stakeholder target
K9.caption: Ask the stakeholder which decision the analysis needs to support.

K10.name: Interlocking data pieces
K10.caption: Match keys and understand the join before combining sources.

K11.name: The analysis toolbox
K11.caption: Know the tools and methods your organisation makes available.

K12.name: The data building
K12.caption: Map the architecture: where data lives, how it flows and who can access it.

K13.name: The bell and its centre
K13.caption: Summarise variation, then reason carefully about samples and uncertainty.

K14.name: The three-way signpost
K14.caption: Think what happened, what may happen and which action could follow.

K15.name: A heart in careful hands
K15.caption: Consider the people affected: fairness, bias, transparency and accountability.

S1.name: A key turning in a shield
S1.caption: Apply legal and organisational controls throughout the data work.

S2.name: Footsteps through the lifecycle
S2.caption: Walk every lifecycle stage in your project and explain what you did.
S2.svg: <path d="M10 12c38-8 48 10 17 22S9 55 52 51M48 46l4 5-4 5"/><ellipse cx="20" cy="16" rx="3" ry="6" transform="rotate(35 20 16)"/><ellipse cx="38" cy="26" rx="3" ry="6" transform="rotate(45 38 26)"/><ellipse cx="22" cy="43" rx="3" ry="6" transform="rotate(-35 22 43)"/>

S3.name: The classification stamp
S3.caption: Assign sensitivity and confidentiality, then apply the right handling.

S4.name: The shape adaptor
S4.caption: Adapt your approach to different data structures and designs.

S5.name: A dashboard under the cursor
S5.caption: Apply domain knowledge and accessible design to the output people use.

S6.name: A repair patch on the table
S6.caption: Identify, resolve or escalate quality problems and check the repaired result.

S7.name: Requirements carried to the finish flag
S7.caption: Trace agreed requirements into the plan and the delivered result.

S8.name: Two streams through a preparation funnel
S8.caption: Join sources, clean them and validate the prepared table.

S9.name: A terminal plugged into a server
S9.caption: Use the tools that connect you to your organisation’s data infrastructure.

S10.name: The calculator and test result
S10.caption: Perform EDA and statistical tests, then interpret the result in context.

S11.name: A model inside a crystal ball
S11.caption: Build a predictive model, evaluate it and use it to inform action.

S12.name: Two voices in conversation
S12.caption: Adapt your message to different stakeholders and listen to their feedback.

S13.name: A calendar with a forecast line
S13.caption: Anchor the forecast in time, evaluate later actuals and explain the horizon.

S14.name: A brush beside the chart
S14.caption: Choose visual representations that reveal quantitative and qualitative findings.

S15.name: The selected tool
S15.caption: Compare the available options and choose the tool that fits the requirement.

B1.name: The locked workstation
B1.caption: Keep your working environment secure through everyday safe handling.

B2.name: A detour around a roadblock
B2.caption: Adapt to a small unexpected obstacle while maintaining productive work.

B3.name: One person connected to a team
B3.caption: Take responsibility for your own work while collaborating with others.

B4.name: A chess knight on logical steps
B4.caption: Build a reasoned sequence of analytical decisions and explain each move.

B5.name: A magnifying glass over roots
B5.caption: Look beneath the symptom, establish the root cause and prevent recurrence.

B6.name: A bending tree with a new leaf
B6.caption: Recover from challenges and carry the lessons into your next attempt.

B7.name: A boat changing course
B7.caption: Change your approach when the project’s scope, goals or responsibilities shift.
